definition: Pathos means a quality that stirs pity or sympathy.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pathos. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pathos should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The shelter's fundraising letter gets its pathos from one line: the terrier still waits by the gate at the hour his family used to come.
Sentiment is milder than pathos — a touch of tender feeling, while pathos genuinely stirs an audience to pity.
Heartbreak goes further than pathos — the audience is no longer just moved to pity but genuinely devastated.

Pity is the ache the audience feels — sorrow stirred by someone else's suffering, the lump in the throat as the lights come up. Pathos sits on the other side of the footlights: not the feeling itself but the quality in the scene that draws that feeling out of a room.

Poignancy is the everyday word for a moment's piercing, bittersweet sting — one photograph, one pause that catches you off guard. Pathos is the critic's term for the same power, and it is broader: in classical rhetoric, pathos names the whole appeal to an audience's emotion.
